Hello,
I am just learing how to use R, but I need to run analysis of the
Human Exon 1.0 st v2 and I have done the low level analysis explained
in the Human Exon Analysis Page. Are there tools in this package that
can help me do this analysis? The first thing I need to do is
Normalize my data to the zero hour time point (two replicates). If
this is not the right place to find out how to do this, where should I
go?

messages.author: 9dda904b2c7a149c
messages.subject: Re: processing data generated by how-to in Exon analysis page
parts:
Hi Ray,

I am assuming you have generated a ChipEffectSet and now want to do
some further analysis on the summarised data. There are not really
any methods for doing this in aroma.affymetrix, but if you extract a
data frame with your summarised expression levels (see the Exon
Analysis vignette again), you will be able to pass these to a package
such as limma. The best place to ask questions about limma is the
Bioconductor list, but if you explain what you are trying to do
(analysis of time series data, by the sounds of it?) then I or others
here may be able to help.

Cheers,

Ken

messages.author: 9dda904b2c7a149c
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: processing data generated by how-to in Exon analysis page
parts:
Hi Ray,

I'm pretty sure extractDataFrame() returns values on the original scale, so you will need to take logs.

So it seems that you want to compare each of your time points (2 reps at each time) to the samples at t=0, presumably to see which transcripts change expression over time.  I would definitely use the limma package to do this.  You could define contrasts (t3-t0, t6-t0, t12-t0, t24-t0, t48-t0) if you are just interested in the different time points compared to the initial time, and fit these to find differentially expressed transcripts.  At this point I would direct you to the limma documentation (which is excellent) and the Bioconductor list, since we are starting to get off-topic for aroma.affymetrix.

Cheers,

Ken
